evidence: unreadable: In seg4:end the last bin's label is cut to "Sin..." in tiny text. In seg4:start the "43% Madagascar" label is too low-contrast to read. In seg3:end Data's head covers the "78%" value, and in seg1:start his body covers the "80%" and "Can't see it" labels.

weakest_scene.visible_evidence: From seg4:start to seg4:end, bins split one whole into Chad 45%, Madagascar 43%, United States 11%, Sin... 1%. Those numbers contradict seg3's 78/75/20/1, they appear nowhere in the narration, and the picture says these countries are parts of one total.
weakest_scene.root_cause: The closing shows per-country rates (the percent of each country with pristine skies) as shares of one whole. Re-normalising them turned the real numbers into made-up ones. The closing line "the lights just won" has no picture that carries it.
weakest_scene.repair_goal: Replace the share bins with a closing picture made of the subject, with Data as the cause. For example, Data flips a light switch and city glow wipes out a field of stars. Use only numbers stated in the story (or none). Every label must sit fully inside the frame at readable contrast.
